children: Australian stock futures point to an uncertain start for the S&P/ASX 200, as traders wait on wage and labor data scheduled for release this week. ASX futures are down by less than 0.1% ahead of Monday's session, suggesting the benchmark index could take a breather after falling 0.7% on Friday. The ASX 200 is still up by almost 2% in November after three consecutive weekly gains. Ahead of the open, coal miner New Hope reported a 3.2% drop in sales across the September quarter. U.S. equities provided a soft lead Friday. The DJIA inched 0.1% ahead, but the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite lost 0.4% and 0.9%, respectively. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
